series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/5] btrfs: use an on-stack path in btrfs_insert_orphan_item()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series modifies the btrfs_insert_orphan_item() function to allocate a path on the stack instead of dynamically, reducing the risk of transaction aborts due to memory allocation failures.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: Approved the patch with a Reviewed-by tag, indicating that it meets code quality standards and is ready for merge.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/5] btrfs: split btrfs_insert_delayed_dir_index() into prealloc and commit phases
series_items.patch_summary: This patch splits the btrfs_insert_delayed_dir_index() function into three separate functions: prealloc, commit, and free. The prealloc function allocates memory for a delayed node and item before modifying the B-tree, allowing -ENOMEM to be returned cleanly if allocation fails. The commit function populates the item data and inserts it into the rb-tree, while the free function releases pre-allocated resources in case of failure. This refactoring improves error handling and reduces the risk of aborting transactions due to memory allocation failures.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested simplifying the btrfs_prealloc_delayed_dir_index() function by returning a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer instead of taking it as an argument, reducing the parameter list.
review_comments.raw_body:
We can directly return a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer, which reduce 
the parameter list.

Otherwise looks good to me.

Reviewed-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>

Thanks,
Qu

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: Author addressed Qu Wenruo's concern about allocating a struct btrfs_dir_index_prealloc on the stack by the caller, and expressed willingness to consider alternative approaches.
review_comments.raw_body:
...but then we'd have to allocate it separately. It's currently
allocated on the stack by the caller. I think we ought to keep it this
way, but I'm willing to be convinced otherwise.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: The reviewer noted that there are only two call sites using on-stack memory for the prealloc structure and suggested converting to a heap memory based solution. Additionally, they pointed out a potential issue with the lifespan management of btrfs_dir_index_prealloc where it is used as an indicator of whether the structure is properly allocated.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledges a concern that NULL pointer means no prealloc is not clear and suggests considering an additional heap allocation, but does not commit to a specific fix.
review_comments.raw_body:
It's a good point. It is more natural to be able to just look and say
"NULL pointer means no prealloc".

OTOH, the entire reason we're doing this is to deal with low-memory
situations. Do we want to add another heap allocation into this
codepath?

Either way, I'll think about it.

Thanks again for the review!
--
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/5] btrfs: pre-allocate delayed dir index before btree modification
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the Btrfs file system by pre-allocating delayed directory indices before modifying the btree. This change prevents ENOMEM failures from leaving the btree in an inconsistent state, which could only be resolved by aborting the transaction. The patch introduces a new parameter to the btrfs_insert_dir_item function for caller-provided pre-allocation and removes a wrapper function that was no longer needed.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that when a pre-allocated delayed dir index is passed to btrfs_insert_dir_item(), and an ENOMEM failure occurs before insert_with_overflow() is called, the pre-alloc memory is leaked because it is not properly released.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that the preallocated memory in btrfs_prealloc_delayed_dir_index() is not utilizing the name->name field, and suggested merging the subsequent memcpy() into this function to avoid unnecessary copying.
review_comments.raw_body:
This is exposed by sashiko.

If we have @prealloc passed in, and before we even hit 
insert_with_overflow(), the previous btrfs_alloc_path() failed, we 
return -ENOMEM directly, leaking the @prealloc.

---

Sashiko also pointed out that, the preallocation itself doesn't really 
utilize name->name.

Thus it may be a good idea to merge the later memcpy() into the 
preallocation function.

Thanks,
Qu

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that additional issues were found by Qu Wenruo and sashiko, agreed to address them in a new version (v3) of the patch series.
review_comments.raw_body:
Good catch. It looks like sashiko also flagged some other similar
issues nearby too that we might as well fix while we're in here. I'll
plan to spin up a v3 and resend the series. Thanks very much for the
review so far!

-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/5] btrfs: handle ENOMEM from btrfs_insert_dir_item() without aborting
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Btrfs kernel code to handle ENOMEM errors from btrfs_insert_dir_item() without aborting the transaction. Instead of aborting, it clears the nlink count and orphans the newly-created inode when memory is exhausted during file system operations such as create(), mkdir(), mknod(), symlink(), and link(). This change allows for more graceful handling of memory pressure situations, preventing potential filesystem corruption.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 5/5] btrfs: pre-allocate delayed dir index for non-overwrite rename
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the Btrfs file system by pre-allocating a delayed directory index before performing non-overwrite renames, allowing for early detection of ENOMEM errors and preventing potential data corruption. The patch introduces a new function to pre-allocate the delayed dir index and modifies existing functions to handle this new parameter. It also preserves the current behavior for overwrite renames by continuing with the transaction even if an ENOMEM error is encountered.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a long-standing issue in the Btrfs file system where memory allocation failures can cause the file system to abort. The patches rework the code to perform memory allocations before critical points, preventing aborts due to ENOMEM errors. This includes changes to directory morphing and orphan handling, with additional tests added to exercise the new behavior. While not all potential cases are covered, this series is designed to work in conjunction with other patches to address remaining issues.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 6.18.y] mm/huge_memory: unlock i_mmap_rwsem before releasing after-split folios

version_history.subject: [PATCH 5.10.y] mm/huge_memory: unlock i_mmap_rwsem before releasing after-split folios

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a use-after-free bug in the Linux kernel's huge memory handling code. The issue occurs when splitting a transparent huge page (THP) that has been poisoned by memory failure, causing the inode to be evicted before the i_mmap_rwsem is unlocked. To fix this, the patch moves the unlock of i_mmap_rwsem to after the remap_page() call, ensuring that all mapping dereferences occur while the folio still pins the inode. This change establishes a new rule for the split function: no inode or mapping dereference should occur once the after-split folios start being unlocked.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 6.18.y] fs/proc/task_mmu: fix PAGEMAP_SCAN written state for unpopulated ptes

version_history.subject: [PATCH 6.12.y] fs/proc/task_mmu: fix PAGEMAP_SCAN written state for unpopulated ptes

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the PAGEMAP_SCAN functionality of the Linux kernel's /proc/task_mmu interface. The issue arises when an unpopulated page table entry (pte) is encountered, and its written state is reported differently depending on whether the fast path or the generic path is taken. To fix this, the patch reports pte_none as written in both paths, ensuring consistency and preventing issues with incremental-dump consumers like CRIU. A selftest has been added to verify the correctness of the change.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 6.18.y] mm/hugetlb: fix swap entry corruption when clearing uffd-wp at fork()

version_history.subject: [PATCH 6.1.y] mm/hugetlb: fix swap entry corruption when clearing uffd-wp at fork()

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's huge page handling code that caused corruption of swap entries when clearing the uffd-wp bit during fork(). The issue arose because the present-PTE bit position was being used to clear the uffd-wp bit, but the swap entries kept the state elsewhere. This led to incorrect updates of the swap offset, which could cause problems later on. The patch fixes this by using the correct function to clear the uffd-wp bit in swap entries and removing the unnecessary clearing of hwpoison entries.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 02/16] selftests/mm: add folio-order check for VA ranges
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function, is_range_backed_by_folio_orders(), to the selftests/mm module. It checks whether a given VA range is backed by folios of exactly a specified order, mapped head-to-tail. The function requires that each order-aligned window of the range maps one such folio, and that the first PFN in each window is naturally aligned with the folio head.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 03/16] selftests/mm: add folio-order detection self-check
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a self-test to verify the accuracy of the vm_util folio-order detection helpers, which are used by khugepaged mTHP tests to detect collapse results. The test faults in memory for each supported anon THP order and checks that the helpers report exactly that order, ensuring they agree with the kernel's understanding of the backing. This patch is part of a larger series of patches and has been verified on x86-64 and arm64 architectures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 04/16] selftests/mm: add order-parameterized khugepaged collapse cases
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds selftest cases to the khugepaged module, which is responsible for collapsing large memory mappings into smaller ones. The new test cases are order-parameterized, meaning they can be run at different memory orders (e.g., 2K, 4K, 8K). This allows testing of the khugepaged collapse behavior at various memory granularities. The patch also includes a new case to test mixed-source folios collapsing. The goal is to ensure that the khugepaged module works correctly across different memory orders and configurations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 05/16] selftests/mm: add khugepaged completion barrier helper
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a helper function called khugepaged_full_pass() to drive the khugepaged daemon synchronously. The function uses a completion barrier to ensure that exactly one full scan pass is completed before proceeding. This is necessary for race and functional tests, which need to set up a layout, let one full scan pass complete, and then check the result. The patch also updates the khugepaged selftest to use this new helper function and ensures that settings are only written when they change.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 06/16] selftests/mm: add khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new selftest, khugepaged_race, to the Linux kernel's selftest suite. The test is designed to exercise the khugepaged feature under contention by introducing multiple threads that fault, use GUP, fork, and mremap concurrently with the khugepaged driver. The test aims to ensure that the khugepaged driver can handle these concurrent operations correctly. The test is configurable and can be run in short or soak mode, depending on the needs of the testing environment.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 07/16] selftests/mm: cover a shared-source collapse write race
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new test case to the selftests/mm/khugepaged.c file, which exercises the requirement that Copy-on-Write (CoW) keeps a shared source isolated from the collapsing side throughout the collapse, even under an actively writing co-sharer. The test case checks that the collapsing child sees the pre-fork content and the writing parent only its own writes. The patch passes on the unmodified kernel and pinpoints the CoW-isolation contract provided by khugepaged collapse.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 08/16] selftests/mm: skip collapse_compound_extreme where the PMD is too large
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies a selftest in the Linux kernel to skip a test case where the PMD (Page Map Directory) size is too large for fault-time THP (Transparent Huge Pages) construction on certain architectures, specifically arm64/64K. The test case is skipped when the hpage_pmd_size exceeds 32M, but MADV_COLLAPSE-driven cases are still exercised to ensure PMD-order collapse functionality is tested on larger configurations. This change prevents the test from failing due to an inability to allocate a large number of pages.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 09/16] selftests/mm: skip khugepaged swap tests when no swap is configured
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series introduces a new selftest for khugepaged, which is a feature that allows the kernel to preallocate huge pages. The test checks if the swap area is configured and skips the swap tests if it's not. This ensures that the test results reflect the actual environment rather than just indicating a missing swap device.

review_comments.author: Mike Rapoport
review_comments.summary: Suggested adding a check for swap configuration to the vm_util module, which would make the code more reusable and useful in other contexts.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 10/16] selftests/mm: verify synchronous khugepaged driving is attributable
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new selftest, khugepaged_sync_check, to verify that synchronous khugepaged driving is attributable. The test uses the huge_memory tracepoints to attribute per-attempt outcomes and checks that exactly one attempt is attributed for each step of the test. The test prepares aligned windows, records source PFNs, runs khugepaged_full_pass() barriers, and requires the window to be collapsed with exactly one attributed attempt. The patch also adds minimal tracefs helpers to vm_util to enable and clear event subsystems and open the trace buffer.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 11/16] selftests/mm: race-harness variant for permissive hole occupancy
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new variant to the selftests/mm/khugepaged_race test, which exercises permissive hole occupancy by selecting hole-heavy windows and allowing racing faults to fill in holes. The test is run with max_ptes_none=0 by default, but can be changed to use the permissive limit with the -z option. This allows for testing of collapsing a window that contains holes, where a racing fault may have filled in the hole before it's re-checked under the page table lock at install time.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 12/16] selftests/mm: add memory-pressure threads to the khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds two new threads to the khugepaged race harness, which exercises memory management functions against faults, pins, fork, mremap, and MADV_DONTNEED. The new threads simulate memory pressure by cycling MADV_PAGEOUT on a dedicated region and triggering compaction through /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory. These additions allow for more comprehensive testing of khugepaged's behavior under various stress scenarios.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 13/16] selftests/mm: parameterize the mixed-source collapse case by source order
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the selftests/mm/khugepaged.c test to parameterize the mixed-source collapse case by source order. The test previously only tested one source order, but this change allows it to test multiple orders, including those that are not exercised deterministically due to the contpte threshold on certain architectures. A new option '-s' is introduced to specify the source order when combined with the existing '-o' target order. This change enables more comprehensive testing of the mixed-source collapse case and helps ensure the correctness of the khugepaged functionality.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 14/16] selftests/mm: zap whole PTE tables in the khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged race harness in the selftests/mm directory to occasionally zap a whole PMD-aligned area instead of individual pages. This is done by introducing a new condition that allows zapping a full table every 64 iterations, which can trigger the empty-table reclaim mechanism and free tables from under parked collapses. The patch aims to improve the test's ability to detect certain types of races between khugepaged and other kernel components.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 15/16] selftests/mm: scale khugepaged's collapse wait with the PMD size
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adjusts the wait time in khugepaged's collapse function to scale with the size of the memory being collapsed. The original three-second timeout was insufficient for large PMDs, causing tests to fail even when the collapse completed correctly. The new approach adds a second per 64M of memory to be collapsed, ensuring that the budget is sufficient for all cases. This change brings the helper function in line with khugepaged_full_pass(), which already allows for longer wait times.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 16/16] selftests/mm: skip khugepaged shmem cases without a PMD page cache folio
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series modifies the khugepaged selftest to skip certain shmem cases where a PMD-sized page cache folio is not supported, which can cause test failures on arm64 configurations.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Suggested removing the cap on page cache folio order, as xas_try_split() can handle non-uniform splits and shmem is already split using this method.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Sun Aug 2, 2026 at 3:52 PM EDT, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>
>
> The page cache caps folio order at MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, and
> xas_split_alloc() puts that cap below the PMD order where a PMD is 512M --
> arm64 with 64K base pages, as include/linux/pagemap.h says outright.
> shmem_huge_global_enabled() then offers no PMD order at all, so
> MADV_COLLAPSE of a shmem range answers -EINVAL and khugepaged passes over
> it.

IIRC, after READ_ONLY_THP_FOR_FS is removed, all pagecache folios are
split using non uniform split, xas_try_split(), so does shmem (except
shmem in swapcache not splittable). In theory, we can get rid of the
cap, since xas_try_split() does not split more than one level like
one can try to make xas_split_alloc() split more than two level (e.g.,
512MB to 64KB on arm64 with 64KB base page).

>
> The shmem cases nonetheless ask for a PMD-sized shmem folio, so on such a
> configuration four of them fail and the run bails out in the middle:
>
> not ok 2 collapse_full not ok 4 collapse_single_pte_entry # Allocate huge
> page...Bail out! madvise(MADV_COLLAPSE): Invalid argument (22)
>
> That is the kernel declining something it deliberately does not support,
> not a collapse defect.  Skip those cases where the PMD order is not a shmem
> order, which thp_shmem_supported_orders() already reports -- it reads the
> same per-size shmem_enabled controls the kernel only publishes for orders
> the page cache can hold.  A tmpfs-backed file argument is skipped on the
> same grounds, and a run left with nothing to collapse into skips outright.
>
> Anonymous collapse is unaffected: its orders are not capped this way, and
> the anonymous cases pass at a 512M PMD.
>
> Assisted-by: Claude-Code:claude-opus-5
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> ---
>  tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c | 21 +++++++++++++++++++++
>  1 file changed, 21 insertions(+)
>
> diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
> index 9213ce1658d0..c5a3c3922581 100644
> --- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
> +++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
> @@ -1584,6 +1584,27 @@ int main(int argc, char **argv)
>  	hpage_pmd_nr = hpage_pmd_size / page_size;
>  	hpage_pmd_order = __builtin_ctz(hpage_pmd_nr);
>  
> +	/*
> +	 * The page cache caps folio order at MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, which
> +	 * xas_split_alloc() puts below the PMD order on arm64 with 64K pages.
> +	 * A PMD-sized page cache folio is then impossible, so the kernel
> +	 * refuses these collapses by design and there is nothing to test.
> +	 */
> +	if (!(thp_shmem_supported_orders() & (1UL << hpage_pmd_order))) {
> +		if (shmem_ops) {
> +			ksft_print_msg("no PMD-order page cache folio: skipping shmem\n");
> +			shmem_ops = NULL;
> +		}
> +		if (finfo.type == VMA_SHMEM && read_only_file_ops) {
> +			ksft_print_msg("no PMD-order page cache folio: skipping tmpfs file\n");
> +			read_only_file_ops = NULL;
> +			read_write_file_read_ops = NULL;
> +			read_write_file_write_ops = NULL;
> +		}
> +		if (!anon_ops && !shmem_ops && !read_only_file_ops)
> +			ksft_exit_skip("Nothing left to collapse into\n");
> +	}
> +
>  	if (anon_target_order &&
>  	    !(thp_supported_orders() & (1UL << anon_target_order)))
>  		ksft_exit_skip("Order %d is not a supported anon THP order\n",




-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series improves the coverage of selftests for khugepaged, a mechanism that collapses huge pages in memory. The patches add new tests and helpers to ensure that khugepaged works correctly across various scenarios, including different page orders, collapse cases, and racing conditions. The changes also include improvements to existing tests and documentation. The goal is to provide a more comprehensive suite of selftests for khugepaged before its underlying mechanism is modified. The patches have been tested on x86-64 and arm64 architectures with 4K and 64K pages, respectively.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about moving the is_backed_by_folio() function to vm_util.c from split_huge_page_test.c, acknowledging that it's a functional change and not just a move. The author confirmed that no functional change is intended.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the range-level question for mTHP collapse tests, which need to check if every order-aligned window of a VA range is backed by one folio of exactly that order, mapped head-to-tail. The author added a new function `is_range_backed_by_folio_orders()` to handle this requirement.
sentiment_signals: acknowledged the need for additional functionality
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

is_backed_by_folio() answers "what order folio backs this page", but
mTHP collapse tests need the range-level question: is every
order-aligned window of this VA range backed by one folio of exactly
that order, mapped head-to-tail?

Add is_range_backed_by_folio_orders(): per window, require a present
and naturally aligned head PFN, a contiguous PFN run across the
window, and is_backed_by_folio() agreeing on the order. A window
assembled from pieces of different folios, or mapping a folio outside
its natural position, fails the check.

Assisted-by: Claude-Code:claude-opus-5
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c | 46 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h |  2 ++
 2 files changed, 48 insertions(+)

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
index 343a15e25a9f..793342095420 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
@@ -365,6 +365,52 @@ bool is_backed_by_folio(char *vaddr, int order, int pagemap_fd,
 	return false;
 }
 
+/*
+ * Check whether the range [start, start + len) is backed by folios of
+ * exactly @order, mapped at their natural alignment.
+ *
+ * is_backed_by_folio() classifies the folio backing one page; here we
+ * additionally require that each order-aligned window of the range maps
+ * one such folio head-to-tail: the VA range must be naturally aligned,
+ * each window's PFN run must be contiguous, and the first PFN must be
+ * the (naturally aligned) folio head.
+ *
+ * This is the check "did this range collapse into order-@order folios":
+ * a window assembled from parts of several folios, or mapping a folio
+ * shifted from its natural position, fails.
+ */
+bool is_range_backed_by_folio_orders(char *start, size_t len, int order,
+				     int pagemap_fd, int kpageflags_fd)
+{
+	const unsigned long nr_pages = 1UL << order;
+	const size_t window = nr_pages * psize();
+	char *vaddr;
+
+	if ((uintptr_t)start % window || len % window)
+		return false;
+
+	for (vaddr = start; vaddr < start + len; vaddr += window) {
+		unsigned long pfn = pagemap_get_pfn(pagemap_fd, vaddr);
+		unsigned long i;
+
+		/* Not present, or not mapping the folio head. */
+		if (pfn == -1UL || pfn % nr_pages)
+			return false;
+
+		for (i = 1; i < nr_pages; i++) {
+			if (pagemap_get_pfn(pagemap_fd, vaddr + i * psize()) !=
+			    pfn + i)
+				return false;
+		}
+
+		if (!is_backed_by_folio(vaddr, order, pagemap_fd,
+					kpageflags_fd))
+			return false;
+	}
+
+	return true;
+}
+
 /* If `ioctls' non-NULL, the allowed ioctls will be returned into the var */
 int uffd_register_with_ioctls(int uffd, void *addr, uint64_t len,
 			      bool miss, bool wp, bool minor, uint64_t *ioctls)
diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h
index 5eb90e0d1d13..76e9938a908e 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h
@@ -97,6 +97,8 @@ int64_t allocate_transhuge(void *ptr, int pagemap_fd);
 int pageflags_get(unsigned long pfn, int kpageflags_fd, uint64_t *flags);
 bool is_backed_by_folio(char *vaddr, int order, int pagemap_fd,
 			int kpageflags_fd);
+bool is_range_backed_by_folio_orders(char *start, size_t len, int order,
+				     int pagemap_fd, int kpageflags_fd);
 
 int uffd_register(int uffd, void *addr, uint64_t len,
 		  bool miss, bool wp, bool minor);
-- 
2.54.0

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the collapse_compound_extreme test failing on arm64/64K due to fault-time THP construction limitations, and added a check to skip this test when hpage_pmd_size > 32M. The patch will still cover PMD-order collapse in MADV_COLLAPSE-driven cases.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

Its fault-time THP construction (x hpage_pmd_nr) cannot hand out a
512M order-13 page on arm64/64K, bailing the whole binary. Skip when
hpage_pmd_size > 32M; MADV_COLLAPSE-driven cases still exercise PMD-order
collapse there. No effect on 4K (2M) or 16K (32M) PMDs.

Assisted-by: Claude-Code:claude-opus-5
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c | 15 +++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+)

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
index 81001e15765c..b43e060b4118 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
@@ -857,6 +857,21 @@ static void collapse_compound_extreme(struct collapse_context *c, struct mem_ops
 	void *p;
 	int i;
 
+	/*
+	 * Builds a PMD's worth of distinct PTE-mapped compound pages by cycling
+	 * hpage_pmd_nr fault-time THPs through mremap. Fault-time THP allocation
+	 * is best-effort, and this needs hpage_pmd_nr PMD-order pages in a row:
+	 * fine at a 2M (4K base) or 32M (16K base) PMD, but a 512M PMD (arm64/64K)
+	 * is an order-13 allocation the allocator cannot reliably hand out even
+	 * once, let alone 8192 times. Cap at a 32M PMD; MADV_COLLAPSE-driven cases
+	 * still cover PMD-order collapse on the larger configs.
+	 */
+	if (hpage_pmd_size > (32UL << 20)) {
+		ksft_test_result_skip("%s: PMD too large for fault-time THP construction\n",
+				      __func__);
+		return;
+	}
+
 	p = ops->setup_area(1);
 	ksft_print_msg("Construct PTE page table full of different PTE-mapped compound pages\n");
 	for (i = 0; i < hpage_pmd_nr; i++) {
--
